papers.title: FerBo: a noise resilient qubit hybridizing Andreev and fluxonium states
papers.abstract: We propose a novel superconducting quantum circuit that should be robust against both relaxation and dephasing over a wide and experimentally accessible parameter range. The circuit consists of a parallel arrangement of a large inductance, a small capacitor, and a well-transmitting Josephson weak link. Protection against relaxation arises from the hybridization between the fermionic degree of freedom associated with Andreev levels in the weak link and the bosonic electromagnetic mode of the LC circuit, hence its name: FerBo. Furthermore, as in the fluxonium qubit, delocalization of the wavefunctions in phase space provides resilience against dephasing.

summary.summary: FerBo is a superconducting qubit combining a high-transparency Andreev weak link with an LC circuit, achieving simultaneous suppression of both relaxation and dephasing through hybridization of fermionic Andreev bound states with the bosonic electromagnetic mode. The qubit states have disjoint support in Andreev sector space and delocalized wavefunctions in phase, providing protection over a well-defined and experimentally accessible parameter regime.
summary.motivation: Conventional superconducting qubits like the transmon and fluxonium suppress either charge noise or flux noise dephasing, but wavefunction delocalization increases coupling to dissipative channels, limiting coherence. Hardware-level protection schemes combining multiple degrees of freedom have stringent parameter requirements; this work explores whether Andreev bound state structure can relax those constraints.
summary.method: An effective Hamiltonian couples the bosonic LC mode to a Josephson quasi-resonant level junction in the even-parity Andreev manifold. Numerical diagonalization and analytical perturbative analysis characterize the qubit's charge relaxation susceptibility $|\langle 0|n^|1\rangle|^2$ and flux dephasing susceptibility $\partial^2 E_{01}/\partial\phi_{\mathrm{ext}}^2$ across parameter space, with support from microscopic Bogoliubov-de Gennes calculations of SNS nanowire junctions.
summary.result: Protection emerges when the circuit impedance satisfies $Z/R_Q \gtrsim 2E_C/(\pi\epsilon_r)$ and the junction transmission is high ($\tau \to 1$), suppressing charge relaxation susceptibility by four orders of magnitude at $\phi_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$ while achieving exponential dephasing suppression; the boundary coincides with an avoided crossing between first and second excited states where the ground and first excited states undergo a parity transition, causing the ground state to localize in the $|-\rangle$ Andreev sector while $|1\rangle$ occupies the $|+\rangle$ sector.

papers.title: Building Block For Universal Continuous Variables Computation In Superconducting Devices
papers.abstract: Continuous variable (CV) quantum computation offers an alternative to qubit-based computing by exploiting the infinite-dimensional Hilbert space of bosonic modes. Despite recent progress, superconducting platforms have yet to demonstrate a scalable architecture capable of universal computation. Here, we design and numerically simulate a two-layer superconducting architecture that implements all five interactions of the universal CV gate set (rotation, displacement, squeezing, Kerr, and beam splitter) within experimentally accessible regimes. To this end, we employ a DC-SQUID as the bosonic mode, a fluxonium qubit to mediate nonlinear interactions, and two ancillary qubits that enable Gaussian and multi-mode operations. By tuning fluxes and frequencies, we achieve high fidelities ($\geq 98\%$) across all gates within state-of-the-art parameter ranges. The modular nature of the design allows straightforward scaling, establishing a feasible pathway toward high-fidelity, universal CV quantum computation based on superconducting circuits.

summary.summary: This work designs a two-layer superconducting architecture implementing all five universal continuous-variable gates (rotation, displacement, squeezing, Kerr, and beam splitter) using a DC-SQUID mode, a fluxonium qubit for nonlinear interactions, and two ancillary qubits. Numerical simulations achieve fidelities $\geq 98\%$ across all gates within state-of-the-art parameter regimes, with gate times ranging from 33 ns (displacement) to 228 µs (Kerr at $\mathcal{F} = 98.8\%$).
summary.motivation: Superconducting platforms currently lack scalable architectures for universal continuous-variable quantum computation, with existing approaches limited by geometric constraints in planar resonator designs or incomplete gate sets.
summary.method: The circuit employs a DC-SQUID encoded as the CV mode ($\omega_m = 10$ GHz) with a fluxonium qubit ($\omega_f = 400$ MHz, $\alpha_f/2\pi \gtrsim 500$ MHz) coupled via tunable quadratic coupling $g_{m,f}(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}})$, and two capacitively coupled auxiliary qubits ($g_{m,i} \approx 104$–105 MHz) for Gaussian operations. Parameters are tuned via external pulses and detunings to realize each gate; fidelities are evaluated on coherent states with $\nu = 2$ (mean photon number $\bar{n} = 4$).
summary.result: Rotation and beam splitter gates achieve $\geq 99\%$ fidelity; displacement is near-perfect; squeezing reaches $\mathcal{F} = 99.8\%$ with $\tau_s = 205$ ns at $g_0 = 8.3$ MHz, $\Omega_S = 150$ MHz; Kerr reaches $\mathcal{F} = 98.8\%$ with $\tau_k \approx 228$ µs at $g_{m,f} \approx 0.83$ MHz—all within demonstrated superconducting coherence times ($T_1, T_2 \gg 100$ µs).
